_about: CONTENT [twenty-five things on the road], 11/2/26 (Paolo 11/2: 'I want more content for the game, more content'; earlier: 'it got pretty boring... a little more quests to do'). THE ROAD'S EVENTS, Battle Brothers' way (reference/library/battle_brothers/: an event stops the company on the road, a face and a situation, two or three choices, a real cost or gain; some remember what you chose and come back later). A modder's file: every event is a row; slices/bohemia_road_events.js reads it and owns no words of its own. WHO: a name and a portrait look (engine/bohemia_crew_faces.js LOOKS: cast_* and faction_*). WHERE: any | paved (the five asphalt road kinds) | rough (rail bed, dry wash) | a district id. WHEN: day | night | any. NEEDS: flag / notflag (a chain), min_day, bats (he must have that many for the event to come), men (crew at least). OPTS: two or three; each option's fx is what happens: bats (+/-), food (+/- a man's night each, the wagon's), gear (a weapon id from records/target/bb/weapons.json, or -1 to lose the bag's newest item), man (+1 joins with {name, look, bg}; -1 one walks), mood ({act, place}: act from records/target/bb/relations.json, place 'near' = the nearest town, or 'faction:<word>'), mins (the clock), flag / unflag (chains), fight ({foe, n, label, win, lose}), chance ({p, yes, no}), quest (a side quest id in BOHEMIA_SIDE_QUESTS.json), say (the speaker's answer). need: what an option asks before it can be chosen. Every word is an attempt, draft:true; the valley's people talk Spanglish, the player's choices are plain English (THE FIRST VOTES: the player does not speak Spanglish). Numbers are shapes TUNING owns.

director.why: Battle Brothers fires a road event every so often on the march, rarely back to back, never in the first moments. Here: never in the first real minute of play (THE SECOND VOTES: nothing happens in the first second; the overworld law: never in the first minute), at least 22 blocks walked since the last one, then a 6% chance each block (about 38 blocks between events on average, two to four an in-game day of steady walking). An event already met waits three in-game days before it can come again (his repeat ruling, 9/5); a chain's events come once.

events.says: Oye, jefe. Two days no food. I don't want batteries, just something to eat. My brother says ask the ones with guns, they got food.

opts.t: Give him two nights of food.

fx.say: Gracias. I don't forget faces. Neither does my brother.
Five. Okay. That's a can at the post. Gracias, jefe.
Sí. Everybody keeps walking.

events.says: You fed my little brother. So I tell you straight: three men sit on the next bend with a rifle. I know a way around. And if you want, I walk with you.

fx.say: Teo. I carry, I watch, I don't complain. Vámonos.
Through the culvert. And there is a dead man's pack down there. Six batteries. Yours.
Your call, jefe. Watch the bend.

who.name: DOÑA PILI
who.from: under a truck with no front wheel

events.says: The axle, mijo. I got the part, I don't got the arms. One hour of your boys lifting and I owe you. A trucker always pays back, ask anybody.

fx.say: Ándale, that's it. I run the Primm road. You'll see me again.

opts.t: Sell her the time: ten batteries.

fx.say: Ten. Pues, fair. Nobody lifts for free no more.
Nobody has time. That's why the trucks stopped.

events.says: ¡Mira quién es! The arms! I been looking for you. A crate of beans fell off the back of my own truck, if you understand me.

fx.say: Six nights for your boys. We're square. Until next time.
Twenty-five, and don't tell my husband.

events.says: (a delivery drone, face-down, its little speaker looping) Paquete en camino. Package on its way. Paquete en camino. The box under it is sealed with the Network's tape.

fx.say: Paquete... en... (the speaker dies. Eighteen batteries in foam, packed like eggs.)

opts.t: Carry it to the nearest town.

fx.say: Gracias por su entrega. Thank you for your delivery. (somebody, somewhere, logged your face.)
Paquete en camino. Paquete en camino.

events.says: Every drone has a camera, amigo. We saw you open our box. You give back eighteen and a little for the trouble, or my friends here come down.

fx.say: Smart. The Network forgets fast when it's paid.

win.say: They dropped their own batteries running.

lose.say: They took fifteen and the drone's camera kept rolling.

events.says: You the one who walked our drone home? Honest people are rare as rain. The Network pays honest. Here.

fx.say: Twenty. And your name is good on our wire now.
News? The Reds move water on the night of the full moon. And eight batteries, because I like you.

who.name: LA TOLLKEEPER
who.from: a shopping cart across the road

events.says: This road is ours today, my loves. Five batteries a head, or ten for all of you because you dress so ugly I feel sorry. Rick Owens would cry.

fx.say: Gracias, gorgeous. Next time you pass, you pass free.

opts.t: Push the cart out of the way.

win.say: The cart had their whole day's take in it.

lose.say: They took the ten anyway, and your hat.

fx.say: Long way is free. Long way is also long.

who.name: LA TOLLKEEPER
who.from: the cart, now with a parasol

events.says: My ugly friends who pay! Go, go, free road. And a gift: the men at the overpass are new and scared. Scared men sell cheap.

fx.say: And five back, because I'm in a mood. Don't get used to it.

opts.t: Buy food off the overpass men.

fx.say: Five nights of food for eight. Told you. Scared.

events.says: Fever three days. My wife went for the clinic, she don't come back. If you got water, a little. If you don't, then just tell her I waited.

opts.t: Leave him a night of food and water.

fx.say: Dios te lo pague. Her name is Lupe. Lupe Ortiz.

opts.t: Carry him to the nearest town.

fx.say: You carried a stranger. People there saw you do it.
I'll tell her a group came by. That's something.

events.says: You're them. He told me. He lived, ¿me oyes? He lived. I got nothing much. I sew. Let me give you something I sewed.

fx.say: A knife, in a sheath I stitched with his old belt. Cut good things with it.
Then I tell everybody in town what you did. That's worth more, maybe.

events.says: (a courier, two days dead, still holding the strap of a bag. The bag has a Remnants seal. A crow looks at you like you're next in line.)

fx.say: Fourteen batteries and a letter nobody will get now. The Remnants count their bags.
The crow waits on a sign the whole time. It does not like you.
The crow goes back to work.

who.name: MADAME BOTTEGA
who.from: a rack of clothes in the road

events.says: Darling. The world ended and you still dress like a parking lot. One coat, Balenciaga, real, from the Forum Shops. Twenty batteries and you live forever.

opts.t: Buy something cheaper: a knife she keeps under the rack.

fx.say: The knife. Tragic. But it matches nothing, so it matches everything.

opts.t: Trade her two nights of food.

fx.say: Food! Fashion eats too, my love. Six batteries and my blessing.
Nobody buys today. Everybody dies ugly.

events.says: Coyotes, big ones, the lab kind. They follow you since the wash. Gimme three batteries and I show you where they sleep. You kill them, the skins sell.

win.say: Skins for fifteen batteries at the post, and meat for two nights.

lose.say: They got into the wagon on the way out.

fx.say: Okay. They're still following you, though.

events.says: The dollar was a false god and it died like one. Now everybody worships the battery. Brothers, give one battery to the Church, and the Church remembers your face at the gate.

fx.say: Five. Bendito. The sisters will hear your name tonight.
...and on the eighth day the screens went dark and man looked up. Gracias for listening. Nobody listens.
Walk, then. The road listens.

events.says: ¡Ayúdame! They say I steal the water, but it's my pump, my father dug it! They're coming. Hide me in your wagon, please.

yes.say: They walk right past. She leaves you three jugs. Three nights of water.

win.say: She gives you the jugs anyway. Her father's pump is hers again tonight.

lose.say: They took her and two of your jugs.

opts.t: Turn her in for the reward.

fx.say: Twelve batteries from the pump men. She doesn't look at you once.
She runs on into the dark.

who.name: A RADIO ON A POLE
who.from: tied with wire, at head height

events.says: (a radio taped to a pole, playing a weather report from before. Sunny. Seventy-two. The dollar is up. Then the same report again. Somebody has been changing its batteries.)

fx.say: Four batteries. The report stops on 'the dollar is'. The quiet is worse.
Sunny. Seventy-two. The dollar is up.

events.says: You took the batteries out of my radio. My wife recorded that report the morning before. It's the last of her voice. Put four back or I follow you forever.

fx.say: Eight. She'll talk for two more weeks. Gracias. Go with God.

fight.label: the radio man and his son

win.say: He doesn't follow you. But you hear the report in your head all night.

lose.say: He takes ten and walks back to his pole.

events.says: We quit the Reds. They make us shoot water thieves, kids, everybody. We fight good. Take us, or don't, but don't tell the Reds you saw us.

fx.say: Benny. The other one goes his own way. The Reds will hear, they always hear.

opts.t: Turn them in to the Reds.

fx.say: Twenty batteries from a Red patrol. The two boys don't fight it.
Gracias. We were never here.

who.name: AN OLD DEALER
who.from: a card table on the median

events.says: One hand, high card. You win, I give you twenty. You lose, I take ten. The house always won, mijo. The house is dead now. Let's see.

yes.say: King. Ay, the king. Take it before I change my mind.

no.say: Seven. Bad night for sevens. Gracias.

opts.t: Ask him about the old Strip.

fx.say: The lights were on twenty-four hours. Nobody looked up. Now everybody looks up. Go on.

who.name: A BRIDE IN SILVER
who.from: a wedding in a parking lot

events.says: ¡Vengan, vengan! A wedding! Two families stop fighting today. Eat, drink, and if you have a gift, the gift table is the truck bed.

fx.say: Ten! You eat like family. Take a plate for the road. The whole town will hear.
Eat, eat. Nobody counts at a wedding. Well. My aunt counts.
Next time, then. There's always a next wedding. Or a funeral.

events.says: Lab cat. American lion, they said, from a bone in Tule Springs. It took my arm and my partner. It sleeps in the wash. Kill it and the reward is yours, I only want to see it dead.

win.say: Thirty batteries, my whole savings. He cries like a kid. Gracias.

lose.say: It's still out there. It knows you now.

fx.say: It will be. It's always everybody's fight, later.

events.says: Good copper in this one, but I need four hands. You help me pull it, we split it. Hour of work. Trades rules, half and half.

fx.say: Half and half, ten each. The Trades will hear you work clean.
¡Rata! I know your faces! The whole Trades will know them!
Pues, more for me.

who.name: A WOMAN IN A WHITE COAT

events.says: Don't be scared. I'm a nurse, I walk at night because the days are too hot. I have bandages and nobody to give them to. Can I walk with you to the next town?

opts.t: Walk her to the next town.

fx.say: Thank you. I'll tell the Volunteers who walked me. We look after the ones who look after us.
Bandages, eight batteries' worth at any post. A fair trade at night.

who.name: A GIRL IN A STORM DRAIN

events.says: ¡Aquí abajo! My foot is stuck in the grate. The water comes when it rains, and it's going to rain. Please.

fx.say: She runs home without saying gracias. Later the whole town knows who did it.

yes.say: She's out. Scraped up, but out. Gracias, gracias.

no.say: It doesn't give. You dig anyway. Forty-five minutes.

events.says: Inspección. What's in the wagon, jefe? We take a tenth of everything, it's the law now. Our law. Or you can try to argue.

fx.say: Eight batteries and a night of food. Pásale. Have a nice day.

yes.say: The jefe laughs. 'You got balls. Go.' Nobody pays.

win.say: Their cash box. Twenty-five. The cartel will want it back.

lose.say: They take twenty and the long way of making a point.

fx.say: Long way around. Smart, maybe.

who.name: A THREE-LEGGED DOG
who.from: and its owner, a very old man

events.says: Chato smells water. Four legs, three legs, he smells it better than any machine. Two batteries and he finds you a cistern nobody knows.

opts.t: Pay two and follow the dog.

fx.say: A cistern under a gas station. Four nights of clean water. Chato wants a scratch.
He likes you. Chato likes everybody. That's his problem.

who.name: THE SMILING MAN
who.from: standing very still in the middle of the road

events.says: (he holds a TV with no back. On it, your own crew, walking this road, from above, ten minutes ago. He smiles.) Everything is recorded. Do you want to see what happens next?

yes.say: Static. Then a picture of a cache under a billboard. It's real. Ten batteries.

no.say: Static. When you look up he's gone, and so are two nights of food from the wagon.

fx.say: He turns his head to follow you. Just his head.

events.says: Raiders hit a farm west of here. We're short a gun. Ride with us one hour, the Blues pay what's fair, and we don't forget who stood with us.

win.say: Twenty batteries and a handshake. The Blues remember.

lose.say: The raiders got away. The sergeant doesn't blame you. Much.

fx.say: Busy. Everybody's busy until it's their farm.
